title: Why Bangladesh descended into violence ahead of Hasina’s planned return

ai.summary: Bangladesh deployed paramilitary forces to contain violence after supporters of ex-PM Sheikh Hasina protested against the government's rejection of her planned return. At least four people died in the week-long unrest, with attacks on police stations, banks, and Muhammad Yunus's ancestral home.

facts.claim: Bangladesh deployed paramilitary troops to help contain a wave of violence
facts.quote: Bangladesh has deployed paramilitary troops to help contain a wave of violence that erupted after supporters of former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina staged protests against the government’s rejection of the ousted leader’s planned return to the country.

facts.claim: At least four people have been killed in the political violence since November 14
facts.quote: At least four people have been killed in the political violence since November 14, including three political activists and a bus worker who died when his vehicle was torched, according to local media reports.

facts.claim: The ancestral home of Muhammad Yunus was set on fire in Chittagong
facts.quote: Late Wednesday, police said the ancestral home of Yunus was set on fire in the port city of Chittagong.

ai.background_note: Bangladesh's government rejected Sheikh Hasina's request for a passport and identity card to return, leading to protests by her supporters that escalated into violence.
